::: {#sol-chebyshev-sample-size}

a.  By @thm-sum-iid-moments, $\Var{S_n} = n\varpar$ for $S_n \eqdef \sumin X_i$,
    so $\samplemean{X}{n} = S_n/n$ has mean $\mean$ and variance $\varpar/n$
    (a constant factor $c$ scales a variance by $c^2$).
    Apply @thm-chebyshev to $\samplemean{X}{n}$ with $k\sdpar/\sqrt{n} = \epsilon$,
    that is, $k = \epsilon\sqrt{n}/\sdpar$, so $1/k^2 = \varpar/(n\epsilon^2)$.

b.  Setting $\varpar/(n \cdot 1^2) \le 0.05$ gives $n \ge 20\varpar$.

c.  See the code below.

```{r}
#| label: chebyshev-sample-size
#| code-fold: false
mpg <- read.csv("data/auto.csv")$mpg
mu <- mean(mpg)
sigma2 <- mean((mpg - mu)^2)
n_min <- ceiling(20 * sigma2)

set.seed(571)
xbar <- replicate(10000, mean(sample(mpg, n_min, replace = TRUE)))
misses <- sum(abs(xbar - mu) >= 1)
normal_approx <- 2 * pnorm(-1 / sqrt(sigma2 / n_min))
c(variance = sigma2, n = n_min, misses = misses, normal_approx = normal_approx)
```

```{r}
#| include: false
# The claims the prose makes: the bound is respected, and it is far from tight.
stopifnot(misses / 10000 <= 0.05, misses <= 5, n_min >= 1)
```

The population variance of `mpg` is `{r} round(sigma2, 1)`,
so $n = `{r} n_min`$ cars suffice.
Out of 10,000 samples of that size, `{r} misses` sample means missed $\mean$ by 1 or more,
against the 5% (500 samples) the bound allows.
The bound is loose because the sample mean of this many cars is nearly normal
(@thm-clt),
and the normal approximation puts the chance of a miss at about
`{r} signif(normal_approx, 2)`;
Chebyshev's inequality must hold for every distribution, as in
@exm-chebyshev-auto.

:::
